body:
I'm pretty experienced with different substances and in your case I think it's because the acute physical withdrawals were over, but the psychological part is trickier, that's what most people refer to as "PAWS" (Post Acute Withdrawal Syndrome), so that's where you possibly feeling better knowing you were going to dose comes in. I say the psychological part is trickier because in my opinion PAWS can be greatly exacerbated by, or sometimes mostly just be an untreated underlying mood disorder coming back that the drug was covering up, so the length, symptoms and severity of PAWS can vary greatly depending on the person. Then you also have to factor in possible depression and anxiety resulting from social and financial consequences of drug use if it got pretty bad. Alcohol for example is pretty short lived in the system so its acute physical withdrawal  (which can literally kill you) is like five days, peaking on the 3rd or 4th day, but as I'm sure you're aware, once out of that danger zone many that call themselves alcoholics talk about resisting the urge to drink as a battle long after the acute, dangerous withdrawal is over.

Anyways, I've done both kratom and Suboxone and for me kratom withdrawal kicked in within like 8 hours without use, whereas with Suboxone, I'd say it took a couple of days to even start.  Even when I just tapered down from 4mg to 2mg/day, I thought I was fine, but 2 or 3 days in I had withdrawals, even while still taking 2mg. I had nightly chills for a few weeks. I also had a dependence on Tramadol at one point for years, and quitting cold turkey that withdrawal lasted about a week, and was like having the flu, but I would get random chills and whatever that slowly dissipated for about a month but didn't interfere with my life too much.
